title: Fundamental limits on state preparation for an open qubit
authors: D. A. Abraamian, L. V. Lokutsievskiy, A. N. Pechen
abstract: We analytically determine the ultimate limits of state preparation in two-level open quantum systems driven by coherent control. For a dissipative qubit governed by a GKSL master equation, we give an exact characterization of the reachable set in the Bloch ball. Dissipation excludes a region of states in the Bloch ball which cannot be approached even under arbitrarily strong coherent driving, and we prove that this region has a nontrivial geometry whose boundary is a surface of revolution around the $x$-axis which is analytic except for two conical singularities. We derive a closed-form control protocol for moving on this boundary, and construct an explicit protocol that steers the system arbitrarily close to any prescribed boundary state. These results provide a complete geometric constructive description of reachable qubit states in the standard dissipative environment, establishing fundamental bounds on controllability and state-preparation fidelity for open two-level quantum systems.
summary: This paper rigorously determines the fundamental boundaries on what states can be prepared in an open qubit system under coherent control. It characterizes this boundary as a specific surface of revolution within the Bloch ball using advanced geometric control theory. The results provide essential, constructive bounds for quantum state preparation fidelity in dissipative quantum computing architectures.
main_problem: The paper aims to analytically determine the ultimate geometric limits of state preparation (the reachable set) for an open qubit subjected to coherent control.
main_result: It proves that the boundary of the reachable set is a surface of revolution around the $r_x$-axis, which is analytic except for two conical singularities. Furthermore, it provides explicit control protocols to approach any state on this boundary asymptotically.
method: The analysis uses geometric control theory applied to the Bloch sphere dynamics governed by a GKSL master equation, involving techniques like analyzing separatrices and constructing specific time-optimal control protocols.
model_or_system: The system is an open two-level quantum system (qubit) whose evolution is described by a Lindblad/GKSL master equation incorporating free Hamiltonian ($\mathrm{H}_0$), coherent driving ($V$), and dissipation rates ($\gamma$).
key_observables: Bloch coordinates $(r_x, r_y, r_z)$ describing the state $ho$, and the boundary surface $\partial R$.
important_parameters: The ratio $\alpha = \gamma/\omega$ (dissipation rate to frequency) is a key parameter governing the geometry of the reachable set.
main_assumptions: Boundary points are only asymptotically reachable in finite time, and the analysis relies on local hyperbolic dynamics near equilibrium points.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the boundary curve $\Gamma$ defining the reachable set's boundary, its intersection with specific planes (like $r_y=0$), and projections of separatrices onto various coordinate planes.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the dynamics in Bloch coordinates, then characterizing the boundary using geometric control theory concepts like separatrices, culminating in the derivation of explicit protocols to approach these fundamental limits.
why_interesting: This work provides a complete, rigorous geometric description of controllability for open quantum systems, which is foundational knowledge for designing robust quantum gates and state preparation routines in realistic noisy environments.
